harnessConsumers.reason: lowerFlatThemeFixture lifts an authored FlatTheme and calls compileTheme directly: it skips ingress (ThemeIntent) and admission, the door compileThemeIntent runs. Each file below leaves when it compiles through the door.

retainedBecause.core/src/infrastructure/compilers/runtim: Measured 2026-09-25: 29 of 34 cases compile through compileThemeIntent; the B-1 block (lowerOver, drills 1-9) stays. Drill 4 grades the lowering clamp, which admission would pre-empt. The block tests lowering internals, not the door.

Through compileThemeIntent the claim is a tenant-document patch over that carried theme, and admission refuses it: Compiled variable count exceeds 512, plus 4 non-hex-ground APCA refusals (button-secondary, sidebar-item-active, light and dark). No first-party baseline bakes the family any more (the adjacent case proves the claim moves 0 channels there), so no admitted intent carries the subject.

unproducedChannelAssertions.law: A positive toContain literal naming a --ds-* channel must have a producer: the shared producer set (libraries/tokens/producers), a runtime write in productive core TS/TSX (object key, typed contract member, bracket assignment, setProperty), a declaration in a committed first-party compile artifact, or a declaration inside the asserting test (a planted drill fixture). Otherwise the assertion pins a dead channel and is a row here.

classes.cut-residue: The family is in a family cut; the cut owns the channel through its readWithoutProducer arm. The row leaves when the cut produces or retires the read.
classes.uncut-family-read: The family is in no family cut, so no work order drains the read. owner stays null until the DT adjudicates ownerProposal (anti-sprawl: a roster admission is an owner decision).

exits.law: A row that left the census is written here with how its test now asserts the paint and the lot that moved it. The gate does not read this list: a test that names an exited channel again without a producer is a new row and red.
